tagline: Road and rail follow the Clark Fork through Lolo National Forest
intro: Montana Highway 135 follows the Clark Fork through Lolo National Forest for 21.5 miles, linking I-90 at St. Regis with MT 200 near Paradise. Visit Montana calls this the St. Regis-Paradise Scenic Byway and highlights the change from open, rolling flats to steep canyon walls. Road and railway initially share the northern bank of the river.
From 1960 to 1978, a secondary route followed the alignment now used by MT 135. It connected U.S. 10 with U.S. 10A, later MT 200, and included a toll-ferry crossing of the Clark Fork.

Leaving St. Regis, the highway heads north and northeast along the river. Near the midpoint, it crosses the Clark Fork and passes beneath the railroad, putting road and tracks on opposite banks. The bends straighten near Quinn, and the highway leaves the national forest before meeting MT 200 a couple of miles east of Paradise.

moments.title: St. Regis
moments.text: Two rivers meet at St. Regis: the St. Regis River joins the Clark Fork here. The town takes its name from the St. Regis River, which Pierre-Jean De Smet named for a fellow Jesuit priest. The post office opened in 1896, and the Northern Pacific Railway built through town in the early 1900s, boosting the local economy. MT 135 begins at I-90 and soon meets the former U.S. Highway 10 at a four-way stop.

moments.title: The river crossing
moments.text: Near the midpoint of MT 135, the road crosses the Clark Fork and passes beneath the railroad. Until this crossing, road and tracks have run together along the northern bank. Beyond it, they follow opposite banks as the highway keeps close to the river’s bends.
moments.notice: Beyond the crossing, road and railroad follow opposite banks of the Clark Fork.

moments.title: Paradise
moments.text: Paradise was a place to reset a railroad watch: crews changed from Mountain to Pacific time here. The community began in 1883 when the Northern Pacific Railroad selected it as a division point. Nearby, the Flathead River enters the Clark Fork. The byway’s MT 135 alignment ends at MT 200 a couple of miles east of Paradise.
